query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a rapid thermal annealing (RTA) treatment under conditions that impose directional (substrate‐induced) strain will drive the nearly equiatomic, single‐phase FeCoNi alloy from its high‐symmetry fcc state into a lower‐symmetry, chemically ordered phase (akin to L1₀ ordering). This ordering, by introducing a tetragonal distortion and enhanced spin–orbit coupling, will increase the intrinsic magnetocrystalline anisotropy and thus elevate the coercivity well above that of the previously studied soft FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt derivatives.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic FeCoNi high-entropy alloy in its as-deposited face‐centered cubic (fcc) state, exhibiting high saturation magnetization and low coercivity.
generation.intervention: Introduce a single processing step: rapid thermal annealing performed on a substrate that enforces a biaxial strain (or includes an externally applied stress field) during the heat treatment.
generation.conditions: RTA conditions (temperature and brief dwell time) must be carefully calibrated on a lattice-mismatched substrate so as to induce directional strain sufficient for chemical ordering while preserving overall high configurational entropy (≥1.0R) and maintaining an almost equiatomic, multicomponent composition.
generation.structural_mediator: The evolution from a disordered fcc lattice to a lower-symmetry, chemically ordered structure (e.g. L1₀-type with a tetragonal distortion) acts as the mediator.
generation.mechanism: Directional strain during RTA promotes long-range chemical ordering and a lattice distortion that lower the crystal symmetry. This change enhances the magnetocrystalline anisotropy via stronger spin–orbit interactions and introduces domain wall pinning centers that boost the coercive field.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the soft ferromagnetic state of as-deposited FeCoNi (and FeCoNiPd/Pt derivatives), the transformed alloy should exhibit a markedly higher coercivity—potentially one to two orders of magnitude larger—while largely retaining high saturation magnetization.
generation.baseline: As-deposited, equiatomic FeCoNi thin films or films processed without the strain-enhanced RTA.
generation.boundary: This effect is expected provided the processing induces sufficient long-range ordering without allowing excessive grain coarsening or reducing the overall configurational entropy below the threshold. Its applicability may diminish if the strain imposed is too low (insufficient ordering) or too high (leading to unwanted phase separation or loss of uniformity).
generation.uncertainty: The precise kinetics of ordering and the coercivity magnitude are not fully known. This proposal builds on evidence showing that RTA and Pt addition can induce an L1₀ phase in FeCoNiMnCu alloys (see PMC11426066, sections Introduction and Results/Discussion) and extends the idea to a simpler FeCoNi system using strain engineering. Uncertainty remains in how effectively similar ordering can be triggered without directly adding Pd or Pt.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a set of equiatomic FeCoNi thin film samples on a lattice-mismatched substrate. Subject one set to the proposed rapid thermal annealing under strain (or with an applied stress field) while keeping a control set unannealed (or annealed without the strain condition). Characterize the crystal structure with X-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy to detect superlattice peaks or tetragonal distortions, and measure magnetic properties (especially coercivity) using vibrating-sample magnetometry.
measurements: XRD to identify the emergence of superlattice reflections consistent with a lower-symmetry (e.g. L1₀) phase
TEM for direct imaging of lattice distortions and ordering
Magnetic hysteresis measurements (VSM) to quantify coercivity and saturation magnetization
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the strain-assisted RTA samples do not show evidence of a chemical ordering-induced lattice distortion (no superlattice features or tetragonal structural change) or if the coercivity improvement is less than one order of magnitude compared to the baseline, then the hypothesis would be refuted.

cited_evidence.text: Certain HEA compositions may exhibit long‐range chemical order through the emergence of multiple sublattices, analogous to high entropy ceramics,[  ] leading to so‐called “high entropy intermetallic” (HEI) compounds.[  ] Previously, transition metal alloys with high anisotropy, such as the L10 phases of FePt and FePd have been achieved by annealing of equiatomic solid solution pre‐cursors.[  ] In the case of metastable high anisotropy phases such as L10 FeNi, unconventional annealing techniques have been employed.[  ] In particular, rapid thermal annealing (RTA) of transition metal alloy films on Si/SiO2 is an effective means of inducing high anisotropy phase formation in solid solution precursors, in part due to the substrate‐induced strain.[  ] In this study, we experimentally demonstrate two thin film HEAs with large coercivity and magnetic anisotropy achieved by RTA. We show that RTA treatment of equiatomic FeCoNiMnCu thin films leads to ≈40‐fold increase in coercivity. By introduction of 50 at.% Pt, we realize an L10 HEI phase of (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy resulting from a reduced lattice symmetry and strong spin‐orbit coupling.
